:J U D G M E N T:
This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 13.10.2019.
2. The averments of the petition is brief is as follows:
On 13.10.2019 at about 3.00 a.m., petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-TC-130 very slowly and cautiously along with his friend.

When they reached near Rangappa Circle, Nandi Hills, Chikkaballapur,
another Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01- EQ-8116 came from opposite direction with high speed in a rash or negligent manner, endangering to human life and dashed against the vehicle in which the petitioner was proceeding.

Due to the said impact,
the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries to his right thigh, eyes and all over the body.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Chikkaballapura Government Hospital,
after first aid, he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and he has undergone surgery for fracture of right femur and insertion of implants.
The petitioner was discharged on 17.10.2019 with an advise to take regular followup treatment and bed rest.
The petitioner has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medicine, nourishment and attendant charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was working as an Assistant Manager in Ujjivan Small Finance Bank, Bangalore and he was drawing salary of Rs.57,500/- per month.
Due to injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner has not attended his work for one month and he has suffered great hardship and mental agony.

The Nandi Giridhama Police have registered the case in Crime No.179/2019 for the offence punishable U/Sec 279, 337 and 338 of IPC against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EQ-8116 for causing the accident.
With these averments petitioner prayed to award compensation.
3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the 1st and 2nd respondents have appeared through their counsel and filed separate written statements.

4. The written statement averments of 1 st respondent are as hereunder:
This respondent has denied the entire petition averments.

Inter-alia contended that,
the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
The offending vehicle was insured with the 2nd respondent as on the date of accident.

5. The written statement averments of 2nd respondent are as hereunder:
The 2 nd respondent has denied the alleged accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, age, occupation, income, cause of accident, nature of injuries,
expenses incurred towards medical treatment by the petitioner.

The 2nd respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EQ- 8116, the liability if any of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that, the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EQ-8116 namely Venugopal @ Gopi was not holding valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
Further, the false complaint has been lodged after the delay of one day against the rider of offending vehicle by colluding with the insured and concerned persons in order to get compensation.
There was no compliance of mandatory provisions of 158(6) of M.V. Act.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.

With these averments,
respondent No.2 prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following:
: I S S U E S:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he sustained injuries on account of rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-01-EQ-8116 by its rider as contended in the petition?
2.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he is entitled for the compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove his case, petitioner himself got examined as P.W.1 and Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 were marked.
Thereafter, P.W.1 was cross-examined from the side of respondent No.2.

R.W.2 was also cross-examined from the side of 2nd respondent.
8. Heard the arguments from both side.

The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent has relied on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka passed in M.F.A.No.6154/2019 (M.V.) between Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi and Others Vs. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd.,

9. ISSUE No.1:-
In order to prove his case, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.

10. In order to substantiate the contentions of written statement, 2nd respondent has examined its Administrative Officer namely Prashanth as R.W.1.
R.W.1 has filed the affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
In support of his evidence, R.W.1 has marked Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.5.
Ex.R.1 is the authorization letter.
Ex.R.2 is the insurance policy.
Ex.R.3 is the notice dated:01.12.2022 issued to the R.C. owner of offending vehicle.
Ex.R.4 is the Acknowledgment due card.

The 1 st respondent also examined as RW-2.
11.

Now, it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that,
the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
12.
According to the petitioner, he has sustained injuries in the road accident.

According to the respondent No.1, the alleged accident was occurred due to negligence of the petitioner himself, the petitioner has filed false complaint by colluding with the police authority against the rider of the motor cycle belonging to the 1st respondent only to get compensation.
According to the 1st respondent the motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA-01-EQ-8116 was not flied on that day.
In order to substantiate the said facts, the 1 st respondent examined himself as R.W.2 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
Except the oral evidence of R.W.2, respondents have not placed any positive evidence in support of their contentions.
Likewise, the respondents neither examined the rider of offending vehicle nor ocular witnesses to the incident to establish their defence.

Moreover,
he has clearly admitted that charge sheet has been filed against the rider of Pulsar bearing Saurabh Suresh Pote vs Arun D.S on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152654867/
4 No.KA-01-EQ-8116.
Therefore, it is crystal clear that, as on the date of accident one Sri. Venugopal was riding the offending vehicle.
13. Further, to prove the alleged negligence on the part of petitioner, the Insurance Company has cross-examined the petitioner/P.W.1 in detail.
Nothing has been elicited from mouth of P.W.1 to establish that the accident was took place only on the negligence of petitioner.
At the cost of repetition, to substantiate its contention, Insurance company has not placed positive evidence.
14. In the instant case, the petitioner has produced police documents.
As per Ex.P.2, complaint was lodged before Nandi Giridhama Police Station.
Thereafter, as per Ex.P.1, FIR was lodged against the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 01-EQ-8116.

On careful perusal of Ex.P.1, Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.7, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the rider of the offending vehicle and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.7 after completing investigation.
A careful perusal of Ex.P.3, it clearly goes to show that, the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.7 i.e.,
charge sheet, it reveals that, the rider of offending vehicle i.e., motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EQ-8116 has been arrayed as an accused.
Hence, the decisions referred to above are aptly applicable to the case on hand.

15. At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveal that, when the petitioner was proceeding on the Yamaha FZ S motor cycle bearing No.KA-01- TC-130, the rider of another motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01- EQ-8116 came in a rash or negligent manner with high and dashed against the motor cycle in which the petitioner was proceeding.
The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EQ-8116 has caused the accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE No.2:- Already this Tribunal has observed that, the accident was caused due to the rash or negligent riding of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EQ-8116.
It is needless to mention that,
1st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The 2nd respondent is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

17. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has averred that, he has sustained grievous injuries to his right leg and other injuries all over the body.
He has produced wound certificate and discharge summary, which were marked as Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.8.
On perusal of these documents, it reveal that, the petitioner has sustained fracture shaft of right femur and the said injury is grievous in nature.
It is relevant to note that, the petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove the disability.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of Future Income due to disabiltiy.
18. Medical Expenses:-

According to petitioner, he has spent Rs.60,000/- towards medical,
nourishment and attendant charges.

In the instant case, the petitioner has produced 12 medical Saurabh Suresh Pote vs Arun D.S on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152654867/
5 bills, which were marked as Ex.P.9.

sentences.text:
On perusal of these documents, it appears to this Tribunal that,
the petitioner has incurred Rs.39,891/- towards medical expenses.
After careful perusal of the medical bills, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for Rs.39,891/- towards medical expenses.
19. Pain and suffering:-
As per Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.8, the petitioner has sustained fracture of shaft of right femur and he has taken treatment as an inpatient from 14.10.2019 to 17.10.2019.
Further it reveals that, the petitioner has undergone surgery in the form of closed reduction with internal fixation of right femur shaft fracture.
As such, the petitioner has suffered a lot of pain and inconvenience.

Considering all these aspects, this Tribunal is awarded compensation of Rs.30,000/-
under the head of Pain and Sufferings.
20. Loss of income during the laidup period:-
The petitioner has produced discharge summary and same has been marked as Ex.P.8.
On perusal of this document, it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for 4 days.
Naturally it shows that, he might have taken atleast one month rest because of the injuries.
The petitioner has averred that, he was working as an Assistant Manager in Ujjivan Small Finance Bank, Bengalur and drawing salary of Rs.57,500/-.
In support of his evidence he has produced Ex.P.10 i.e., his computer generated pay slip.
To substantiate the contents of Ex.P.10, the petitiner neither examined his employer nor produced any other documents such as oppointment letter or bank bass book.

Hence, this Tribunal taken the notional income of petitioner as Rs.14,000/- per month by relying on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another.
Hence, one month is to be considered as loss of income during laidup period.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.14,000/- as compensatin under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
21. Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges:-
According to the petitioner, he has spent Rs.60,000/- towards medical, nourishment and attendant charges.
The petitioner has not produced any documents in this regard.
In so for as food, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatinet for about 4 days.

Hence,
looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner,
he is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,000/- under the head of Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges.
22. Loss of future amenities and happiness:- The petitioner was aged about 23 years at the time of accident.
The petitioner has not examined the medical witness to show that, he has sustained any disability and physical deformity due to accidental injuries.
Therefore, he is not entitled for compensation under this head.
23. Future medical expenses:- The petitioner has not stated anything towards future medical expenses.
Hence, he is not entitled any compensatin towards future medical expenses.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs.87,891/-.
25. Regarding liability and interest.
Driving License:- According to respondsent No.2, the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EQ-8116 had no valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
The insured/1 st respondent has entrusted his vehicle to the said driver by violating the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contention of the 1st respondent is that, after due investigation, the police have filed the charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle under Sec.181(3) of M.V. Act.
Hence, the 2 nd respondent is not liable to pay compensation.
In order to substantiate the said contention, the 2nd respondent has examined R.W.1.
R.W.1 has reiterated the written statement averments in his affidavit evidence in-lieu of examination-in- chief.
Further he has deposed that, their counsel has issued legal notice by calling upon the respondent No.1 to produce the driving licence of the rider of offending vehicle namely Venugopal @ Gopi.
The respondent No.1 has not produced the driving licence.
26. Now the next question before this Tribunal is whether the rider of the offending vehicle was having valid DL or not?.
In this connection, it is worth to take Ex.P.7 for discussion.
A careful perusal of this document, the police have filed charge sheet for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 of I.P.C. and also Sec.181(3) of M.V.Act.
Further, the charge sheet discloses that,
Venugopal @ Gopi has been arrayed as accused

. Further, charge sheet reveals that, the said Venugopal @ Gopi drive the offending vehicle without having valid D.L. Therfore, it is crystal clear that, respondent No.2 has established that, the respondent No.1 has allowed the unauthorized person to drive the vehicle.
In other words, insurance Company has placed cogent and corroborative evidence to prove that, rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. at the time of accident.
Moreover respondent No.1, who is the R.C. owner of the above vehicle has contested the case and examined himself as R.W.2.

But he has not produced any document to show that, the rider Saurabh Suresh Pote vs Arun D.S on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152654867/
7 of offending vehicle had valid and effective D.L. at the time of accident.

sentences.text: Hence, this Tribunal come to conclusion that, at the time of accident, the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EQ-8116 had no valid and effective D.L. to drive the said vehicle.
As per Ex.R.2, the policy was in force.

27. At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.30131/2021 dated: 12.05.2020 between New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Yallavva and Others held that, "the charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: In the circumstances, applying the principles of law has held in the judgments referred (Supra) "pay and recover" is to be ordered.
It is to be held that, the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.

As the offending vehicle was duly covered by the policy issued by the insurer as on the date of accident, the insurer shall satisfy the award to the claimant in the first instance and is at liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle".
28.

Apart from that, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Amrit Paul Singh and Another Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. and Others reported in 2018 (7) SCC 558, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held at para 24 that, "the Tribunal as well as the High Court had directed the insurer was required to pay the compensation amount to the claimants with interest with the stipulation that the insurer shall be entitled to recover the same from the owner and the driver.

entities.text: Amrit Paul Singh and Another Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. and Others reported in 2018 (7) SCC 558
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The said directions are in consonance with the principles stated in Swarna Singh and Others cases pertaining to pay and recovery principle".
29.

By relying on the judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court, and also the Full Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, the 2nd respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization and further the 2nd respondent-insurer is at liberty to recover the award amount from the 1 st respondent-R.C. owner of the offending vehicle in accordance with law.
Accordingly, Issue No.3 is answered in the partly Affirmative.
30. ISSUE No.4:- In view of discussions made above, I proceed to pass the following:

:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the petition.
Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.87,891/- (Rupees Eighty Seven Thousand Eighty Hundred and Ninety One only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
It is clarified that, the insurer- 2nd respondent is at liberty to recover the award amount from the 1st respondent-owner of the offending vehicle in accordance with law.

Hence,
looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner,
he is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,000/- under the head of Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges.
The petitioner has not examined the medical witness to show that, he has sustained any disability and physical deformity due to accidental injuries.
Therefore, he is not entitled for compensation under this head.
Hence, he is not entitled any compensatin towards future medical expenses.

Therefore, it is crystal clear that, as on the date of accident one Sri. Venugopal was riding the offending vehicle.
Nothing has been elicited from mouth of P.W.1 to establish that the accident was took place only on the negligence of petitioner.
14. In the instant case, the petitioner has produced police documents.
On careful perusal of Ex.P.1, Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.7, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the rider of the offending vehicle and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.7 after completing investigation.
A careful perusal of Ex.P.3, it clearly goes to show that, the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Further, on perusal of Ex.P.7 i.e.,
charge sheet, it reveals that, the rider of offending vehicle i.e., motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EQ-8116 has been arrayed as an accused.
1st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The 2nd respondent is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
He has produced wound certificate and discharge summary, which were marked as Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.8.
On perusal of these documents, it reveal that, the petitioner has sustained fracture shaft of right femur and the said injury is grievous in nature.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of Future Income due to disabiltiy.
Further contention of the 1st respondent is that, after due investigation, the police have filed the charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle under Sec.181(3) of M.V. Act.
Hence, the 2 nd respondent is not liable to pay compensation.
. Further, charge sheet reveals that, the said Venugopal @ Gopi drive the offending vehicle without having valid D.L. Therfore, it is crystal clear that, respondent No.2 has established that, the respondent No.1 has allowed the unauthorized person to drive the vehicle.
In other words, insurance Company has placed cogent and corroborative evidence to prove that, rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. at the time of accident.
Moreover respondent No.1, who is the R.C. owner of the above vehicle has contested the case and examined himself as R.W.2.
But he has not produced any document to show that, the rider Saurabh Suresh Pote vs Arun D.S on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152654867/
7 of offending vehicle had valid and effective D.L. at the time of accident.
Hence, this Tribunal come to conclusion that, at the time of accident, the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EQ-8116 had no valid and effective D.L. to drive the said vehicle.
